Vocabulary help Key terms Words for this lesson Use these definitions when you need help with a term. cytokinesis Division of the cytoplasm into separate daughter cells. cleavage furrow An inward constriction of an animal cell during cytokinesis. cell plate A developing partition that contributes to the new wall between dividing plant cells. cell-cycle checkpoint A control mechanism that helps determine whether a cell proceeds to a later stage.
Choose an answer Acrosome Cleavage furrow as the only mechanism Cell plate
Choose an answer Rapid division can be part of normal controlled growth Plant cells never contain DNA Cancer means any cell in metaphase
Show the explanation No. Division frequency and capacity differ among cell types.

Vocabulary help Key terms Words for this lesson Use these definitions when you need help with a term. meiosis I The first meiotic division, in which homologous chromosomes separate. synapsis Pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I. tetrad A paired set of two replicated homologous chromosomes containing four chromatids. reduction division A division that reduces chromosome sets from diploid to haploid, as in meiosis I.
Choose an answer DNA bases from their sugars Homologous chromosomes Sister chromatids in every chromosome
Show the explanation No. Homologue pairing and segregation reduce chromosome sets in meiosis I.

Open required check · Meiosis I and separation of homologous chromosomes Explain what you have learned This check counts toward chapter progress. Correct the 2 selections to unlock 2 written explanations. Saving writing records your response; it does not grade its accuracy. Start Redo this check Not started Required chapter check Selection 1 Why is a cell after meiosis I haploid even though its chromosomes remain replicated? It has already completed fertilization It has no centromeres It has one homologue of each chromosome type It contains only one DNA molecule total Check answer Selection 2 What makes a tetrad different from one replicated chromosome? A tetrad contains no DNA A tetrad is always four unreplicated gametes A tetrad is a single RNA molecule A tetrad contains two replicated homologues and four chromatids Check answer Answer the selections correctly to unlock the writing. Written explanations Written explanation 1 Explain how meiosis I reduces chromosome number without separating sister chromatids. Maximum 3200 characters. Explain the biology in your own words. Save written response Compare after saving your own response Homologous pairs align and the two homologues move to opposite poles during anaphase I. Each future daughter receives one chromosome of each pair, so it is haploid. The sister chromatids within each chromosome remain together until meiosis II. Check your explanation for: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities. Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result. Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports. Written explanation 2 For a 2n = 8 species, describe chromosome and chromatid counts after meiosis I. Maximum 3200 characters. Explain the biology in your own words. Save written response Compare after saving your own response Each cell has n = 4 chromosomes. Each chromosome is still replicated, so there are 8 chromatids per cell. The cell is haploid because it has one homologue of each type, not because the chromatids have separated.
